content.mandatory_action: It is important to check baby's growth regularly and have it marked in the CHDR.
content.weighing_schedule: The child should be weighed every month until the 2nd birthday.
content.length_milestones: Length should be measured at least at 4, 9, 12, and 18 months.

content.parental_resource: Parents are encouraged to read the yellow pages in the CHDR for guidance.
content.support_system: Ask your Public Health Midwife or doctor to explain anything you do not understand or want to know more about.

content.alert_conditions: According to the CHDR, if the child is overweight, underweight, or has growth faltering, special nutritional advice is required.
content.professional_referral: Parents must take advice from healthcare staff if growth trends deviate from the standard curve.

content.ebf_duration: Exclusive breastfeeding is required until the completion of 6 months (180 days).
content.transition_protocol: Immediately after 180 days, complementary foods should be introduced in addition to breast milk.
content.extended_breastfeeding: Breast milk should be continued for 2 years and beyond.

content.physical_milestones: Between 9-12 months, the child should be able to sit without help and stand by holding onto furniture.
content.communication: The child begins to imitate sounds and can pronounce simple words with meaning.
content.cognition: The child can understand simple instructions, such as 'clap hands' or 'wave goodbye'.

content.mobility: Provide the child with safe opportunities to walk around the house.
content.play_and_learning: Allow the child to turn pages in a book and involve them in family meal times.
content.language_development: Use correct words when describing objects to the child and talk about things seen in daily life.

content.motor_skills: The child can walk without support and can throw a small ball.
content.vocabulary: The child should be able to say at least 2-3 words.
content.body_awareness: The child can identify at least one part of their body (nose, mouth, eyes) when asked.

content.physical_activity: Allow the child to climb stairs under supervision.
content.self_care: Give the child opportunities to try taking off their own clothes.
content.communication_style: Ask simple questions and use clear, simple language to explain things.

content.walking: The child can walk and run without help.
content.construction_play: The child can build a tower using 2-3 blocks.
content.language: The child uses about 10 words and can form a simple sentence of at least 2 words (e.g., 'Daddy come').

content.balance: Help the child learn to stand on one foot to improve balance.
content.creativity: Provide opportunities for the child to draw circles, straight lines, and faces.
content.hygiene: Encourage the child to start using the toilet, but do not use force.

content.advanced_motor: The child can run and climb stairs without help.
content.art_skills: The child can draw a circle or a curved shape.
content.complex_speech: The child can build sentences with 3 or more words.

content.active_play: Give the child a chance to jump using one foot.
content.sorting: Allow the child to play with toys that can be grouped by color or shape.
content.social_skills: Encourage the child to wash their own feet and hands.

content.stability: The child can stand on one foot.
content.dressing: The child can put on shoes and clothes, although they may struggle with buttons.
content.literacy_prep: The child can copy simple patterns and counts up to three objects.

content.timing: BCG vaccine is given at birth.

content.protection: Protects against Polio, Diphtheria, Whooping Cough, Tetanus, Hepatitis B, and Hib.

content.doses: Polio (OPV) 2, fIPV (Fractional Inactivated Polio Vaccine), and Pentavalent 2 are administered.

content.growth_checks: Growth should be checked monthly until the 2nd birthday and marked in the CHDR.
content.length_checks: Length is measured at 4, 9, 12, and 18 months.

content.parental_interaction: During meals, point out food names, colors, and tastes to stimulate brain development.
content.child_experience: Active interaction makes the child love meal times while enhancing learning.

content.positive_reinforcement: Use positive words and encourage the child instead of negative commands like 'don't do that'.
content.shaming_warning: Avoid talking about the child's faults to others in front of the child.

content.punishment_warning: Physical punishment (hitting, pulling ears) is not an effective method of discipline and causes mental issues.
content.behavioral_focus: Reject the bad behavior, but do not reject the child.

content.skin_to_skin: Hold the baby close immediately after birth to keep them warm and encourage breastfeeding within the first hour.
content.disease_protection: Colostrum (first milk) protects the baby from various diseases.

content.urgent_symptoms: Seek immediate medical help if the baby is unusually quiet, crying excessively, or refusing to breastfeed.
content.umbilical_care: Keep the umbilical cord clean and dry.

content.intro_phase: Start with 2-3 teaspoons of well-mashed rice at 6 months.
content.diversity_7_months: Introduce dhal, pumpkin, carrot, liver, and fish gradually.

content.fever_management: Control fever before offering food as a feverish child will refuse it.
content.extra_nutrition: During recovery, give an extra meal and extra breastfeeds for 2 weeks.

content.serving_style: Rice and curries can be served separately and mixed while feeding.
content.portion: Provide 3/4 tea cup of food, 3-4 times a day.

content.main_meals: 3 main meals a day, each slightly more than a tea cup.
content.diversity: Include 5 different types of vegetables and fruits daily.

content.schedule: Vitamin A megadose is given every 6 months starting from age 6 months until 5 years.
content.worm_treatment: Worm treatment is provided every 6 months starting from age 18 months.

content.dose: Measles, Mumps, and Rubella (MMR) 1 is administered.

content.doses: Polio (OPV) 4 and DPT (Triple) booster are administered.

content.dose: Measles, Mumps, and Rubella (MMR) 2 is administered.

content.doses: Polio (OPV) 5 and DT (Double) booster are administered.

content.common_effects: Mild fever or swelling at the injection site is normal and does not require special treatment.
content.severe_reactions: Severe reactions are very rare, but if they occur, contact the Public Health Midwife or doctor.

content.registration: As soon as you return home after delivery, inform the Public Health Midwife of your area.
content.visit_schedule: The midwife will visit the home on day 10, between days 11-28, and on day 42 to provide advice.

content.breast_milk_composition: Breast milk contains all the nutrients needed for the baby's growth during the first 6 months.
content.feeding_frequency: Feed the baby as often as they desire, both day and night.

content.bonding: Hold the baby with love and sing songs/lullabies to them.
content.visual_stim: Keep colorful toys within the baby's eye level to improve focus.

content.technique: If a child is out of control, giving them 'time' (removing them from the situation to a quiet space) can help them calm down.
content.consistency: Both parents must agree on the methods used to discipline the child.

content.portion: A child aged 1-2 years should consume 1 egg per day.
6-8 sprats should be included in the daily diet.

content.meat_fish: Two matchbox-sized pieces of fish, chicken, meat, or liver daily.
content.kunissan: Alternatively, 2 tablespoons of Kunissan (small shrimp) can be given.

content.portion: 3-6 tablespoons of cooked dhal, green gram, or cowpea daily.

content.variety: 3-6 tablespoons of different types of vegetables.
content.greens: Half a tea cup of green leafy vegetables daily.

content.milk_products: 1 cup of curd or yogurt daily.

content.staples: 2 cups of rice, milk rice, string hoppers, hoppers, or thosai throughout the day.

content.portion: Fruit twice a day (e.g., one medium banana and one orange).

content.definition: Snacks are nutritious foods rich in energy and nutrients, taken in small amounts.
content.purpose: They give extra energy and nutrients in a small volume of food.

content.examples: Boiled potato with butter, boiled egg, yogurt, or local yams with coconut.

content.posture: The baby can lift their head and chest when lying on their stomach.
content.focus: The baby can follow a moving object with their eyes.
content.social: The baby begins to recognize and smile at their mother.

content.posture: The baby can hold their head up steadily while sitting.
content.hand_eye: The baby can reach for and hold objects with both hands.
content.vocalization: The baby begins to make 'cooing' sounds and laughs out loud.

content.mobility: The baby can sit by themselves and may start to crawl.
content.manipulation: The baby can transfer an object from one hand to the other.
content.cognition: The baby begins to understand that hidden objects still exist (object permanence).

content.adverse_effects: Formula milk in the 1st year can have adverse long-term health effects.
content.introduction: The decision to introduce formula milk should only be made by a doctor.

content.monitoring_frequency: Weigh the child every month regardless of age if growth issues are present.

content.parental_agreement: It is vital for both parents to have a consensus on discipline methods.

content.first_food: Very well mashed rice mixed with expressed breast milk.

content.yolk_first: Start with a small bit of boiled egg yolk first, two weeks after starting solid foods.
content.white_later: Introduce boiled egg white about one week after the yolk.

content.texture: Coarsely chopped texture for main meals.
content.finger_foods: Soft center portion of a hopper, bread with butter, or ripe avocado.

content.supervision: Do not leave the baby alone with finger foods.

content.amount: 3/4 tea cup of food at each meal.

content.additives: Add oil or thick coconut milk as usual to keep meals energy-dense during illness.

content.amount: 1/2 tea cup of coarsely mashed rice per meal.

content.hydration: Offer sips of boiled, cooled water after main meals or snacks.

content.amount: Half a tea cup of food, 2-3 times a day.

content.fruit_portion: About 4 teaspoons of well-mashed fruit after main meals or as a snack.

content.amount: Half a tea cup of coarsely chopped food, 2-3 times a day.

content.fruit_portion: 4-5 tea spoons of scraped fruit after main meals.

content.frequency: 1-2 snacks a day between main meals.

content.language: The child can use complex sentences and express past, present, and future.

content.motor_skills: The child can jump on one foot and draw a simple person with head and body.

content.tip: Maintain eye-to-eye contact when talking lovingly to the baby during feeds.

content.environment: Feed the baby in a designated place with minimum distraction.
content.movement_warning: Do not feed the baby while they are walking around the house or garden.

content.frequency: Three main meals per day plus 1-2 snacks.

content.tip: Temper food with 1-2 tea spoons of oil or butter to increase energy content.

content.rationale: Animal foods provide iron which is critical for brain development in the first 2 years.

content.texture: Transition from very well mashed to coarsely mashed rice by age 7 months.

content.initial_breastfeeding: Initiate breastfeeding within the first hour of birth.
content.colostrum_benefit: Colostrum (initial milk) is essential as it protects the baby from various diseases.
content.exclusive_duration: Provide only breast milk until the completion of 6 months; no other liquids are necessary.

content.midwife_registration: Inform the area Public Health Midwife immediately after returning home following delivery.
content.visit_timeline: The midwife typically visits on day 10, between days 11-28, and on day 42 to examine the mother and baby.

content.umbilical_cord: The umbilical cord must be kept clean and dry at all times.
content.daily_cleaning: If the baby is healthy, they should be cleaned or bathed daily.

content.danger_signs: Seek immediate medical care if the baby shows unusual silence, excessive crying, refusal to breastfeed, or a foul-smelling umbilical cord.
content.temperature_alerts: Fever or abnormally low body temperature are critical warning signs in a newborn.

content.BCG_vaccine: Administered at birth to protect against tuberculosis.
content.side_effects: Mild fever or swelling at the injection site is normal and does not require special treatment.

content.18_month_booster: OPV 4 and the DPT (Triple) booster are given at 18 months.
content.5_year_booster: OPV 5 and the DT (Double) vaccine are administered upon completion of 5 years.
content.11_year_vaccine: The ATD vaccine (Adult Tetanus and Diphtheria) is given at 11 years.

content.teething_age: The first milk tooth usually appears between 6-12 months (average 9 months).
content.full_set: A child typically has a full set of 20 milk teeth by 2.5 years of age.
content.dental_delay: If no teeth appear by 12 months, consult a dental surgeon.

content.brushing_initiation: Start brushing as soon as the first tooth emerges, twice a day.
content.fluoride_toothpaste: Use a small smear of fluoride toothpaste after the child reaches 12 months of age.
content.parental_assistance: Parents should assist with brushing until the child is about 7 years old.

content.sugar_restriction: Limit sugary foods to minimize the risk of tooth decay (cavities).
content.night_feeding: Avoid letting the child sleep while breastfeeding or bottle feeding to prevent tooth decay.

content.behavioral_focus: Address and reject the bad behavior, but never reject the child.
content.consistent_rules: Both parents must agree on and maintain consistent disciplinary methods.
content.physical_punishment_warning: Physical punishment like hitting or pulling ears is ineffective and harmful to a child's mental health.

content.license_mandate: A child development center must obtain a license or temporary permit from the Provincial Department of Probation and Child Care Services before establishing[cite: 191].
content.validity_period: A license for a child development center is valid for only three years from the date of approval[cite: 195].
content.renewal_timeline: Renewal applications must be submitted at least three months prior to the expiry of the existing license[cite: 207].

content.under_5_ratio: There must be at least 1 staff member for every 5 children under 5 years of age[cite: 314].
content.over_6_ratio: There must be at least 3 staff members for every 25 children over 6 years of age[cite: 315].
content.gender_policy: Only female caregivers and managers should be recruited for centers providing care for girls[cite: 233].

content.internal_space: Each child must be provided with 40 sq. ft. of internal bedroom space[cite: 536].
content.bed_spacing: The distance between two beds should be two feet, with one foot of extra space around each bed[cite: 542].
content.mosquito_nets: A mosquito net must be provided for every bed[cite: 541].

content.toilet_ratio: One toilet must be provided for every 8 children[cite: 560].
content.bathroom_ratio: There should be at least one bathroom for every 10 children, equipped with one shower and one wash basin[cite: 577].
content.privacy_locks: Every toilet and bathroom must have a lockable door[cite: 574, 578].

content.last_resort: Institutionalization should be considered a last resort only after all possible alternatives fail[cite: 418].
content.economic_prohibition: Institutionalization must never occur solely due to economic problems[cite: 420].
content.adoption_review: For orphaned or abandoned children under 14, the possibility of adoption should be considered[cite: 428].

content.annual_monitoring: Monitoring of child development centers is conducted annually by the National Child Protection Authority[cite: 988].
content.grading_system: Centers are classified into Red (immediate intervention), Yellow (needs improvement), and Green (satisfactory) categories based on supervision marks[cite: 993].
content.red_category_followup: Red Category centers must be supervised again within two weeks of the initial assessment[cite: 996].

content.liquor_restriction: Liquor outlets must not be located within 100 meters of a child development center[cite: 503].
content.perimeter_security: There should be a high wall or protective fence around the center to prevent unauthorized entry[cite: 676].
content.security_personnel: A security guard must be present at all times to ensure child safety[cite: 678].

content.school_attendance: All children of compulsory school age (16 years or less) must be sent to school regularly[cite: 879].
content.vocational_training: Children beyond compulsory education age should be referred for vocational training courses at their discretion[cite: 862].
content.disability_access: Designing of premises should be accessible to children with disabilities in accordance with national regulations[cite: 533].

content.role_models: Staff members must always serve as role models for the children[cite: 323].
content.substance_ban: It is strictly prohibited for staff to bring drugs, tobacco, or alcohol into the center premises[cite: 326].
content.confidentiality: Staff members are obligated to protect all confidential information regarding the children[cite: 251].

content.menu_display: The daily menu for the children must be kept on display in the center[cite: 619].
content.child_participation: At least five children above age 10 should participate in making decisions regarding daily menus[cite: 622].
content.monitoring_meals: Staff must closely monitor children during meal times[cite: 634].
